newsitem.title: USA: Chilly week forecast for U.S. Midwest crop areas.
newsitem.headline: Chilly week forecast for U.S. Midwest crop areas.

text.p: Another chilly week was forecast for the U.S. Midwest with low temperatures near freezing, but meteorologists doubt crops will be hurt.
"We are not at this time anticipating temperatures low enough to damage the soft red winter wheat crop," said Joel Burgio, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp.
However, he said should these lows extend south to where the wheat was more mature, some damage could be done.
Temperatures this past weekend dipped into the low 30 degrees Fahrenheit from Iowa and southern Minnesota to Ohio, but Burgio also doubted these lows hurt crops.
Freezing weather also dipped into western Nebraska and northwest Kansas, but Burgio doubted the hard red winter wheat crop was hurt.
"It is pretty certain the Midwest will have cooler than normal weather most of the week," said Marshall Wickman, meteorologist with Wilkens Weather.
But Wickman said any freezing or sub-freezing temperatures in the Midwest would be isolated and unlikely to significantly damage crops.
Scattered showers were forecast for the Midwest this week as well as sections of the Plains, but should miss the dry wheat areas of western Kansas.
"The northwest and central sections of Kansas do need rain, but they are not going to get any," said WSC's Burgio.
High temperatures across the central Plains should fluctuate this week from the high 60s to low 80s.
Both Burgio and Wickman expected the cool weather pattern to continue across the northern Plain and Midwest through next week.
